Investing.com - Oppenheimer downgraded Bill.com Holdings Inc. (NYSE:BILL) to Perform from Outperform on Friday following the company’s announcement of an acquisition agreement.

Bill.com announced Friday an agreement to be acquired by TPG in partnership with Corpay for $6.0 billion, or $63.25 per share. The transaction represents a 31% premium to the 60-day weighted average price through November 16. The stock surged 17.6% over the past week following the announcement, trading at $64.08, near its 52-week high of $66.58.

The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Lacerte will remain CEO following the close of the transaction.

Oppenheimer removed its $60 price target on the acquisition announcement. The firm views the transaction as comparable to AvidXChange’s takeout multiples at 3.8 times calendar year 2026 sales and 15.7 times adjusted EBITDA, while Bill.com’s deal values the company at 4.1 times calendar year 2027 sales and 11.4 times EBITDA. Notably, InvestingPro analysis suggests the stock remains undervalued even at the acquisition price, with 19 additional ProTips available including insights on the company’s impressive 84% gross profit margins and strong recent momentum.

The firm expects investor focus to shift toward the approval process and closing timeline, with standalone execution remaining relevant primarily if the deal should fail.

In other recent news, Bill.com Holdings Inc. reported its first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings, which led to Truist Securities raising its price target on the company to $58 from $50 while maintaining a Hold rating. The firm adjusted its financial model, increasing its fiscal 2027 core revenue forecast by about 1%. Meanwhile, Susquehanna downgraded Bill.com to Neutral from Positive, citing M&A uncertainty, despite noting the company’s strong operational performance with a 38.7% adjusted operating margin. In contrast, William Blair upgraded the stock to Outperform, highlighting Bill.com’s potential for monetization and margin expansion.

Additionally, BMO Capital raised its price target on Bill.com shares to $68 from $56, motivated by acquisition speculation involving TPG. UBS initiated coverage with a buy rating, setting a price target of $64, and praised the company’s growth outlook in the business-to-business payments sector. These developments reflect varied analyst perspectives on Bill.com’s future trajectory amid its current market activities.
